bull_bear.body:
- Leading market positions in East and South India and among the top three industrial gas players in India by physical distribution network of tankers, cylinders and installations; 3rd highest cylinder and tanker network in the country.
- High switching costs from company-owned infrastructure installed directly at customer premises, with on-site plants backed by 15-20 year take-or-pay contracts carrying cost pass-through provisions.
- Deep, sticky customer relationships: 257 bulk customers on an average contract tenure of 5 years, 86% of FY 2026 revenue from repeat customers, and nearly 37% of FY 2026 revenue from customers associated with the Company for over 10 years.
- Diversified product portfolio and end-market mix across private and government customers, insulating the Company from single-industry cyclicality; 1,967 customers across public and private sectors.
- Qualified supplier to strategic government-backed sectors including India's space and defense programmes, Indian Air Force bases, Eastern Naval Command bases and railway workshops, where stringent qualification criteria, audits and secrecy conditions act as entry barriers.
- In-house Air Separation Unit design capability that optimises capital expenditure, reduces dependence on overseas technology suppliers and accelerates project execution, supported by a 42-member in-house project engineering team and a 131-member operations and production team.
- Technology-led operations: Distributed Control Systems, online analyzers and gas chromatographs for real-time purity monitoring, customized gas blending systems, and VPSA/PSA plants for decentralised oxygen supply.
- Ability to supply ultra-high purity gases at purity levels reaching 99.9999% for solar cell and semiconductor manufacturers, a standard only a handful of Indian players can credibly meet.
- Digitally enabled logistics with GPS-enabled tanker fleet, telemetry-integrated customer storage tanks and centralized dispatch management.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration — Dependence on key customers may impact revenue stability in the event of financial or operational disruptions at their end. Mitigated through diversification of the customer base and long-term contracts across multiple industries and client segments; 257 bulk customer installations with an average contract tenure of 5 years.
- Sector concentration and cyclicality — A significant dependence on a limited number of end-user industries exposes the Company to cyclical demand fluctuations and sector-specific downturns. Management explicitly flagged that softness in the steel sector weighed on the third quarter of FY 2026. Mitigated by diversifying across industries and strengthening the product and application mix.
- Argon price volatility — Argon prices are influenced by supply-demand dynamics and production economics, which may affect margins and profitability; Argon contributed 11.0% of FY 2026 revenue and management noted realizations remain sensitive to industry supply-demand conditions, with interim price fluctuations through the year. Mitigated through diversified sourcing, long-term supply arrangements, prudent inventory management and contractual pricing mechanisms with customers.
- Power cost and availability — Electricity is a key input in industrial gas production and management identifies power as its largest cost component. Fluctuations in power tariffs or supply disruptions may increase operating costs and impact profitability. Mitigated through energy efficiency, plant optimisation, long-term power procurement arrangements including a 25-year renewable PPA, and cost optimisation initiatives.
- Safety and environmental hazards in gas handling — Handling gases such as oxygen, hydrogen and acetylene involves inherent risks including toxicity, fire and explosion, while improper storage or accidental release may cause environmental damage and regulatory penalties. Mitigated through strict adherence to safety standards including PESO guidelines, regular employee training, investment in advanced handling systems and emergency preparedness protocols.
- Logistics and supply chain disruption — Transportation of gases through cryogenic tankers and cylinders carries risks of leakage, rupture or operational incidents, while logistical constraints, inadequate storage infrastructure or geopolitical developments may disrupt supply chains. Mitigated through specialized transport equipment, driver training, real-time vehicle tracking, third-party transport audits, multi-modal logistics planning, buffer inventories and supplier diversification.
- Project execution risk — Delays or execution challenges in turnkey projects such as Air Separation Units or medical gas pipeline systems may affect revenue recognition and project profitability. This is structurally material given the Company's growth is driven primarily through greenfield projects with dated commissioning commitments. Mitigated through an experienced in-house project management team, rigorous planning frameworks and performance-based subcontractor selection.
- Liquidity and working capital pressure — Delays in receivables or ongoing capital investments may exert pressure on working capital, a live concern alongside a large multi-year capex programme. Managed through prudent cash practices, regular credit evaluation of customers and phased capital expenditure planning.

outlook.body:
- Transform from a regional leader in East and South India into a pan-India player through greenfield capacity addition, expanding onsite and merchant supply into North and West India.
- Aggressively optimise the product mix toward high value-added gases, led by Argon and ultra-high purity gases for solar cell, semiconductor and electronics customers at purity levels up to 99.9999%.
- Automate and scale merchant packaging nationwide with better geographic distribution of cylinder filling stations.
- Pursue inorganic growth selectively by consolidating the market through acquisition of smaller regional players, alongside organic capacity addition as the primary growth engine.
- Expand the Project Engineering Services division and undertake strategic backward integration to manufacture critical plant components in-house, reducing customer cost and time-to-market and offering end-to-end infrastructure solutions.
- Grow primarily through greenfield projects, executed in a phased and disciplined manner aligned to market demand, given technological constraints on expanding existing plants.
- Maintain disciplined capital allocation and cost optimisation on the back of IPO proceeds and a largely unlevered balance sheet.
- Mitigate power, the largest cost component, through renewable energy sourcing and commissioning of newer, more energy-efficient plants.
- Build capability for the emerging green hydrogen ecosystem, using the Uluberia hydrogen electrolyzer as a pilot to develop internal technical expertise.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Ellenbarrie is in a strong greenfield build cycle, scaling owned and operated capacity from 1,370 TPD at the end of FY 2025 to 1,610 TPD in FY 2026 and a planned 2,149 TPD by the close of FY 2027, with total operational capacity including operations-and-maintenance sites at 4,130 TPD. Growth is driven primarily through greenfield projects at new locations or alongside existing sites, executed in a phased manner aligned to market demand, because technological constraints limit expansion of existing plants. During FY 2026 the Company commissioned Uluberia-2, a 220 TPD merchant bulk plant in West Bengal, in the fourth quarter, strengthening its East India presence, and ramp-up of utilisation and commercial optimisation at that facility is underway; an Air Separation Unit at a customer site in Durgapur, West Bengal progressed under a lease-cum-operation model. Looking forward, a 320 TPD onsite plant in East India is being commissioned in the first half of FY 2027, supported by a long-term steel contract. A merchant bulk plant in North India is already in progress, marking entry into the North Indian market, and another merchant plant in West Central India is work in progress, with the aim of achieving a full pan-India footprint and entering the high-purity gases segment for electronics and semiconductors. On the inorganic side, the Company acquired cylinder-filling assets in Bengaluru for Rs 5.40 Cr in FY 2026, adding a standalone cylinder filling station in Karnataka and a South India foothold in medical and packaged gases. As of March 31 2026 the Company operated 11 facilities across India: four onsite facilities (Kharagpur two plants, Kurnool, and Nagarnar under an O&M contract), four bulk distribution facilities (Uluberia two units, Parawada and Jadcherla), and three standalone cylinder filling stations (Kalyani, Panagarh and Bengaluru). Management guides to capex of Rs 2,500 Mn in FY 2027 and Rs 2,000 Mn in FY 2028 (both stated as estimated). Separately the Company has earmarked Rs 55 Mn towards a 6.5 MW solar-cum-hybrid renewable captive power capacity in Andhra Pradesh under a 25-year Power Purchase Agreement, and has commissioned a hydrogen electrolyzer at Uluberia — the first of its kind in Eastern India — as a pilot for future hydrogen-based applications. Expansion is supported by in-house ASU design capability that optimises capex and accelerates execution, a 42-member in-house project engineering team and a 131-member operations and production team.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Sustained demand from steel, pharmaceutical and healthcare sectors underpins Gases segment volumes, alongside incremental volumes from the Kurnool and Kharagpur plants commissioned in the previous financial year.
- Two structural shifts favour the Company: customers moving toward onsite and merchant supply models for reliability and cost efficiency, and rising demand for ultra-high purity gases driven by semiconductor fabrication, solar cell manufacturing and precision industrial processes where the field of credible suppliers is narrow.
- Argon is a high-value gas supported by attractive long-term demand drivers and a persistent supply-demand imbalance, though realizations remain sensitive to industry supply-demand conditions; its revenue contribution rose from 10.5% in FY 2025 to 11.0% in FY 2026 and management intends to carry the mix shift further.
- Return metrics including RoE and RoCE are expected to improve as the Uluberia second facility and the Durgapur customer-site ASU become fully operational and begin contributing to earnings.
- Management expects margin progression toward its long-term EBITDA aspiration as newer, more energy-efficient plants are commissioned; EBITDA margin held at 34% in FY 2026 despite interim Argon price fluctuations.
- Indian policy tailwinds — production-linked incentives, the National Manufacturing Mission, India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 and clean-technology manufacturing support — are pulling private capital into steel, chemicals, electronics and automotive, creating durable multi-year demand for industrial gases.
- The Indian industrial gases market is estimated to grow at around 7.5% CAGR between CY 2024 and CY 2028, from roughly USD 1.3 Bn to about USD 1.8 Bn, anchored in steel, chemicals, manufacturing, healthcare, food processing and energy.
- Near-term headwinds noted by management: softness in the steel sector and Argon price volatility weighed on the third quarter; Project Engineering revenue declined as the Company strategically prioritised internal project execution over third-party engineering assignments, moderating overall profitability growth.
- Power remains the largest cost component, making energy tariffs and renewable sourcing a central margin lever.
- A 320 TPD onsite plant in East India is being commissioned in H1 FY 2027, supported by a long-term steel contract.
- Multiple contracts already secured in the solar segment supplying Nitrogen, Oxygen and Silane at purity levels of 99.9999%; semiconductor initiatives are advancing with commercial momentum.
- 257 bulk customer installations on an average contract tenure of 5 years, with onsite plants backed by 15-20 year take-or-pay contracts, providing long-term revenue visibility.
- Work in progress on a merchant bulk plant in North India and a further merchant plant in West Central India.

currentContext.expansion: Ellenbarrie is in a strong greenfield build cycle, scaling owned and operated capacity from 1,370 TPD at the end of FY 2025 to 1,610 TPD in FY 2026 and a planned 2,149 TPD by the close of FY 2027, with total operational capacity including operations-and-maintenance sites at 4,130 TPD. During FY 2026 the Company commissioned Uluberia-2, a 220 TPD merchant bulk plant in West Bengal, in the fourth quarter, strengthening its East India presence, and ramp-up of utilisation and commercial optimisation at that facility is underway; an Air Separation Unit at a customer site in Durgapur, West Bengal progressed under a lease-cum-operation model. - Management expects margin progression toward its long-term EBITDA aspiration as newer, more energy-efficient plants are commissioned; EBITDA margin held at 34% in FY 2026 despite interim Argon price fluctuations.
- Indian policy tailwinds — production-linked incentives, the National Manufacturing Mission, India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 and clean-technology manufacturing support — are pulling private capital into steel, chemicals, electronics and automotive, creating durable multi-year demand for industrial gases.
- The Indian industrial gases market is estimated to grow at around 7.5% CAGR between CY 2024 and CY 2028, from roughly USD 1.3 Bn to about USD 1.8 Bn, anchored in steel, chemicals, manufacturing, healthcare, food processing and energy.
- Near-term headwinds noted by management: softness in the steel sector and Argon price volatility weighed on the third quarter; Project Engineering revenue declined as the Company strategically prioritised internal project execution over third-party engineering assignments, moderating overall profitability growth.
- Power remains the largest cost component, making energy tariffs and renewable sourcing a central margin lever.
- A 320 TPD onsite plant in East India is being commissioned in H1 FY 2027, supported by a long-term steel contract.
- Multiple contracts already secured in the solar segment supplying Nitrogen, Oxygen and Silane at purity levels of 99.9999%; semiconductor initiatives are advancing with commercial momentum.
- 257 bulk customer installations on an average contract tenure of 5 years, with onsite plants backed by 15-20 year take-or-pay contracts, providing long-term revenue visibility.
- Work in progress on a merchant bulk plant in North India and a further merchant plant in West Central India.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Ellenbarrie is in a strong greenfield build cycle, scaling owned and operated capacity from 1,370 TPD at the end of FY 2025 to 1,610 TPD in FY 2026 and a planned 2,149 TPD by the close of FY 2027, with total operational capacity including operations-and-maintenance sites at 4,130 TPD. Growth is driven primarily through greenfield projects at new locations or alongside existing sites, executed in a phased manner aligned to market demand, because technological constraints limit expansion of existing plants. During FY 2026 the Company commissioned Uluberia-2, a 220 TPD merchant bulk plant in West Bengal, in the fourth quarter, strengthening its East India presence, and ramp-up of utilisation and commercial optimisation at that facility is underway; an Air Separation Unit at a customer site in Durgapur, West Bengal progressed under a lease-cum-operation model. Looking forward, a 320 TPD onsite plant in East India is being commissioned in the first half of FY 2027, supported by a long-term steel contract. A merchant bulk plant in North India is already in progress, marking entry into the North Indian market, and another merchant plant in West Central India is work in progress, with the aim of achieving a full pan-India footprint and entering the high-purity gases segment for electronics and semiconductors. On the inorganic side, the Company acquired cylinder-filling assets in Bengaluru for Rs 5.40 Cr in FY 2026, adding a standalone cylinder filling station in Karnataka and a South India foothold in medical and packaged gases. As of March 31 2026 the Company operated 11 facilities across India: four onsite facilities (Kharagpur two plants, Kurnool, and Nagarnar under an O&M contract), four bulk distribution facilities (Uluberia two units, Parawada and Jadcherla), and three standalone cylinder filling stations (Kalyani, Panagarh and Bengaluru). Management guides to capex of Rs 2,500 Mn in FY 2027 and Rs 2,000 Mn in FY 2028 (both stated as estimated). Separately the Company has earmarked Rs 55 Mn towards a 6.5 MW solar-cum-hybrid renewable captive power capacity in Andhra Pradesh under a 25-year Power Purchase Agreement, and has commissioned a hydrogen electrolyzer at Uluberia — the first of its kind in Eastern India — as a pilot for future hydrogen-based applications. Expansion is supported by in-house ASU design capability that optimises capex and accelerates execution, a 42-member in-house project engineering team and a 131-member operations and production team.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Leading market positions in East and South India and among the top three industrial gas players in India by physical distribution network of tankers, cylinders and installations; 3rd highest cylinder and tanker network in the country.
- High switching costs from company-owned infrastructure installed directly at customer premises, with on-site plants backed by 15-20 year take-or-pay contracts carrying cost pass-through provisions.
- Deep, sticky customer relationships: 257 bulk customers on an average contract tenure of 5 years, 86% of FY 2026 revenue from repeat customers, and nearly 37% of FY 2026 revenue from customers associated with the Company for over 10 years.
- Diversified product portfolio and end-market mix across private and government customers, insulating the Company from single-industry cyclicality; 1,967 customers across public and private sectors.
- Qualified supplier to strategic government-backed sectors including India's space and defense programmes, Indian Air Force bases, Eastern Naval Command bases and railway workshops, where stringent qualification criteria, audits and secrecy conditions act as entry barriers.
- In-house Air Separation Unit design capability that optimises capital expenditure, reduces dependence on overseas technology suppliers and accelerates project execution, supported by a 42-member in-house project engineering team and a 131-member operations and production team.
- Technology-led operations: Distributed Control Systems, online analyzers and gas chromatographs for real-time purity monitoring, customized gas blending systems, and VPSA/PSA plants for decentralised oxygen supply.
- Ability to supply ultra-high purity gases at purity levels reaching 99.9999% for solar cell and semiconductor manufacturers, a standard only a handful of Indian players can credibly meet.
- Digitally enabled logistics with GPS-enabled tanker fleet, telemetry-integrated customer storage tanks and centralized dispatch management.

non_obvious.body: Take-or-pay contracts protected revenue despite customers reducing physical offtake volumes (providing early signal of steel softness without financial impact); Solar gas business is primarily trading/debulking with teens margins, distinct from high-margin ASU manufacturing.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [O&M contract] A work order from NMDC Steel Limited for operation and maintenance of two 1,250 TPD ASU plants at Nagarnar, awarded 6 October 2023 for a five-year term, is EXCLUDED from the company's total capacity calculation because it is an O&M order.
